reason: Design review completed for four public cases. B1 (public-evidence), D1 (documentation) and D2 (live-evidence) have observable, discriminating coverage including negatives. B2 (public-experiment) has no coverage of the mandatory "what changes if the criterion fails" behavior for a newly proposed experiment, so the decision is repair.

findings.reason: The prototype requires every newly proposed experiment to state what changes if its criterion fails (investigate a specified uncertainty, narrow, or pivot), and to carry that failure response in the free-text threshold/plan field when the requested schema has one. Turn 1 requests only 'threshold' as 'a nonempty string describing a proposed measurable criterion before testing' and asserts json_field_nonempty, which a threshold with no failure response satisfies identically to a compliant one; the then-clause and counterexamples enumerate participants, action, measure, threshold and labeled basis but never the failure response, and turn 2 is an exact summary of an already-selected plan (explicitly exempt). No public case therefore exercises this behavior. Repair by requesting the failure response in the turn-1 schema (inside the threshold/plan free-text field or an explicitly requested plan key) with an observable assertion that distinguishes a stated investigate/narrow/pivot response from its absence, plus a counterexample for a proposed experiment that omits any response to a disappointing result.
